summary: Canadian Coast Guard light on North Ballenas Island off Parksville, BC: station 1900, moved 1912, concrete tower 1917, de-staffed 1996; closed, boat access only.

structures.note: White octagonal tower with red lantern and gallery; built about 400 yards north of the 1900 wooden tower (LighthouseFriends).
First tower, on South Ballenas Island; taken down and rebuilt on North Ballenas in 1912; superseded in 1917 (LighthouseFriends).

access.note: Grounds and tower closed; reached only by boat (Lighthouse Directory; LighthouseFriends).

facts.ownership: Light station federal (Canadian Coast Guard); the rest of the island privately owned, per the Lighthouse Directory.

events.note: Square pyramidal wooden tower on South Ballenas Island, 10 m (33 ft) to the vane (LighthouseFriends).
Station established 1900 (Lighthouse Directory); LighthouseFriends says the light was completed in 1900.
Hand foghorns set up on 15 September 1901 at five Pacific lightstations, Ballinac Islands among them.
Fog-alarm building completed during the fiscal year ending 31 March 1908 (report printed 1909); diaphone plant supplied for $1,900.
Wooden tower taken down on South Ballenas Island and rebuilt near the fog alarm on North Ballenas.
Reinforced concrete tower with triple-flash reflector built about 400 yards north of the wooden tower.
De-staffed on 1 September 1996; last keeper transferred to Cape Scott (LighthouseFriends). Lighthouse Directory calls the station automated.

keepers.name: William Henry Brown
keepers.note: Listed at Ballinac Island, appointed 3 October 1901 in the 1903 list (read from the page image, printed p. 69; the 1908 list gives the same entry); LighthouseFriends gives 1901 to 1911 and says he was appointed when the light was completed in 1900. Committed to the New Westminster asylum from 1905-06 per LighthouseFriends.

keepers.note: Also spelled Betiat in LighthouseFriends. LighthouseFriends calls him Brown's nephew in one passage, and says in another that Maggie later married him, an immigrant who had anglicised his name to William Brown. Not reconciled.

corrections.why: The 1900 date belongs to the first wooden tower on South Ballenas Island, moved in 1912 and superseded in 1917. The 11 m octagonal concrete tower in the record was built in 1917.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikidata's 1917 is the year the present concrete tower was built and lit; the Lighthouse Directory's 1900 is the year the station was established with the first wooden tower. Both describe different structures, and the 1917 date is confirmed by the Department's report printed in 1918.

Wikipedia places the light on West Ballenas Island. The Canadian Coast Guard list and LighthouseFriends both place it on the north point of North Ballenas Island, which matches the record's coordinates. The Coast Guard list is used here. Wikipedia is not cited.

notes_for_editor: Verified on page images this pass: the 1903 list (printed p. 69, scan 246) reads Brown, Wm. Henry, Ballinac Island, Oct. 3, 1901; the 1908 list (printed p. 148, scan 155) gives Brown at Ballinac Island from Oct. 3, 1901 and Gurney at Pine Island; the 1918 report (fiscal 1916-17, printed p. 41, scan 48) puts the reinforced concrete tower, triple-flash reflector, day labour, on the Ballenas Island row. Fiscal periods: the 1902 report is for the year ended June 30, 1901; the 1903 for the year ended June 30, 1902; the 1908 volume for the nine months ended March 31, 1907; the 1909 volume for the fiscal year ending March 31, 1908; the 1918 volume for fiscal 1916-17. (1) First keeper's start: LighthouseFriends says 1900 (light completed); the 1903 Marine list says 3 October 1901. The story states both and does not settle it. (2) Wikipedia places the light on West Ballenas and says parts of the island are provincial park or Crown land (lead only, not cited). CCG and LighthouseFriends place it on North Ballenas, as the record does; the Lighthouse Directory says the island is privately owned except for the light station, and the story uses that. Ownership still needs a human check. (3) LighthouseFriends is internally inconsistent on the family: Betait as Brown's nephew, versus Maggie later marrying Betait, who had anglicised his name to William Brown. The story states both; the record keeps 'nephew' as LighthouseFriends's main account. A human should decide. (4) Only Brown's 1903 entry is a table entry used in the story. The 1911 to 1914 keeper tables read by column position are not used. (5) The Estevan and Newington entries (1918 report, printed p. 234) and the Leehro entry (printed p. 235) are narrative, not tables. An earlier draft gave the machinery delivery to the Leehro; corrected to the Newington. (6) LighthouseFriends uses an outdated term for Maggie's status; the story does not reproduce it. (7) No wrecks or rescues are sourced for this station in the sources read. (8) Newspapers not searched: BC papers are not in Chronicling America. (9) Commons photograph in the record has no licence in the record; none added.
